data: The Lives and Afterlives of Great Books

New course description: "This course offers a foundation in literary studies, through the medium of great books, and their reception across time. Engaging questions of what constitutes a great book, canonization, intertextuality, and methods for reading, we will study some of the greatest and most influential works of literature in translation, adaptation, and discursive dialogue. This class is reading-intensive, and of particular importance to students in the humanistic disciplines. Each iteration of the course will focus on a single intellectual, literary or performance genealogy, be it through the centering of specific texts, or through specific concepts, genres, or media. In Trimester 1 of the 2026-27 academic year, students will close-read and interrogate the Greco-Roman Homeric intertextual canon, with the Iliad as our core text. All students must purchase physical copies of the required texts for the course, without exception, due to the annotative nature of assignments.
